blocks.x: Hi. Your name please? Abby Arnold.
Your date of birth and place of birth? September 25, 1937 in Baptist Hospital of New Orleans.
Have you been to New Orleans all your life? Yes. When did you first come to where there was such a folk music as New Orleans Jazz?
I think for as long as I can remember. As long as you can remember?
What did you think of it when you first came?
I didn't think anything of it when I first heard it because it was all around me.
When you first thought about it, did you just like it?
Naturally I always liked it because my father had a great deal to do with it and he played it more so than any other kind of music and so it just became more or less part of me.
He played instruments or he played records?
Both. He played the piano then he had other people in to play other instruments and then he has a pretty good collection of it on records.
What would you say your friends would think of it?
I think most of my friends...
Oh, I thought of it then I should say.
Well, thought of it then. That was back around when I was...
When you first started going out to parties.

When we first started going out to parties it was just about the only form of music as far as my friends were concerned. That it was the only kind of band that we would consider getting for a good time and it was the only kind of music that we would go all the way down to the French Quarter to listen to.
Would you say most of the parties you went to then... About what age was this when we started going out?
From between 14 to 17 high school years.
Would you say most of the parties then tended to have jazz bands?
Definitely.
What bands would they have usually?

Well, they usually have Celestine and then... And then for serious dances like sorority dances every once in a while they would have pop bands which never were accepted with too much enthusiasm. But it was just sort of the style that when you were going to have a serious dance you had to have semi-serious music.
In other words, jazz wasn't thought to be socially high brown enough for...
Not socially high brown enough but at times not in keeping with long evening dresses and tuxedos. But not that it carried any social stigma as far as acceptable music for parties went.
What did your parents and your parents contemporaries say about it?
Oh, they were strictly for jazz and nothing else as far as party music. There were only two kinds of music as far as they were concerned, classical music and jazz.
Not your parents, what about your parents' friends?
Well, most of my parents' friends thought the same way. They've always been great jazz enthusiasts.
Alright. How old are your parents then? Uh...
Uh... My father's in his early 50s, my mother's in her late 40s. Uh...
Well, uh... Have you noticed that he changed in attitude towards jazz since when he first started going out since about age 14?
Do you mean among my contemporaries and my parents?
No. Not among young contemporaries. Yes. And with you too.
Yes. It's branched out into other forms of jazz, progressive jazz and all that. It's still considered one of the best forms of party music though. Uh...
That's what most of you think would be one of the best forms of party music.
Yes.
Uh... Did... Have you ever thought of it as... Just as part... Did you think of it just as part of music or have you ever thought of it as an art form? Uh...

I thought of it as an art form only in the... In its greatest musicians and I don't think that its greatest musicians are in New Orleans anymore. I think that Celestan's band for one can be considered one of the best jazz bands in the country but not as a... Uh... Not on a program that you would sit and listen to. I think you can hear the best jazz at a party because I think... I think that... Part of jazz is... It's reactions... In... It's audience... And that comes best at a party atmosphere rather than a concert atmosphere. But still I think that there are great jazz artists in the world that I would just sit and listen to rather than dance to. And...
That would be New Orleans jazz. Would you mean New Orleans jazz? I'm talking about New Orleans jazz.
As it is in New Orleans now or as it has originated in New Orleans?
New Orleans jazz is in New Orleans jazz tradition. As it is in New Orleans now also as it was in New Orleans.

Well if you're speaking of people like Louis Armstrong, Sidney Bichet, and Kid Ory and those who I think they are some of the greatest jazz artists in the world and that they rate sitting and listening to either on records or in person. But I think that jazz as it is now in New Orleans has strictly become more a form of music to be enjoyed rather than to be set... to sit and listen to it seriously. Okay. Alright. For one thing the best artists get paid more out of New Orleans than they do in New Orleans.
Well, when you... you said jazz was the most popular form of music when you were in high school. What about you in college? In New Orleans? And when you go...
Well, I think Rock and Roll was coming to the fore as party music. And I think it is now. Because it's earthier. Because it's earthier.
Well, what? In some ways you would say... the attitude about your friends and your parents and their friends jazz is a social example for music and...
Oh, definitely. I think that people still look forward to a party with jazz much more than they would look forward to a party with any form of... of... um... pop music.
Oh, my God. Now they have to tend to refer to that a little more than when you and your friends...
Yes, because it makes for a wilder party. But...
Which you prefer... to listen to and go to dance and dance to it. Which you prefer?

Well, it depends strictly on the mood and on the type of party. I think that a... a beer drinking rowdy party is best with a rock and roll band. I think a party with... a great variety of people with... with a great variety of ages, all of them respond to... to jazz because it seems to be a... much commoner medium than... than rock and roll is. And I think everyone will have fun at a... a party with... with New Orleans jazz, whereas only the... strictly the younger people will have fun at a party with rock and roll. Wow. But if you're speaking of jazz as a serious form of listening to music, well... among the people who look at... at... music at all consider it... from a serious... artistic standpoint, I think they definitely do consider jazz... worthy... to be... listened to.
I think... most of the people... the majority of New Orleans people with your acquaintance would have that idea, you think?
The ones who consider music seriously at all... would... would enjoy sitting down and listening to... a good... jazz artist.
Do you think there's anything else you could add on the... topic of social... acceptance into all this jazz by New Orleans... acceptance and acceptability?

Well, I think that the social acceptance of... New Orleans jazz by New Orleans is... is strictly based upon... New Orleans... love for a good time. And that jazz has always represented a good time. And it still represents a good time. And... even though rock and roll, which is only a degenerate form of jazz... has... come to the floor lately... It still... can't replace jazz completely... as good time music.
Anything else?

Well... the bit about... listening to it... seriously... I think that... there are few people anyway... in New Orleans... among my... who... who... sit down... and give a lot of time to listening to music anyway... and I think among those who do... they will appreciate the fact that there are many jazz artists... who are worth sitting down and listening to.
